Map orientation and source scale are inadequate to resolve the slight source/render endpoint displacement into different physical terminal classes.

The supplied terminal class sea is preserved as supplied metadata. The inspected historical map places both selected endings within a narrow pale, rock-flanked inland passage rather than establishing an ordinary open-coast river mouth. No geometry or metadata correction follows.
No present surface or subglacial hydraulic continuity, selected lake throughflow, surveyed river length, Korean name or formal-register status is established.

terminal_review.observation: The final short northwestward sequence occupies the narrow pale, bedrock-flanked inland passage. Both separately supplied terminal positions were considered on the original. The source endpoint is slightly southwest of the rendered endpoint; the rendered position is slightly northeast in the same ordinary mapped setting. The map scale does not resolve their small separation into distinct physical end conditions. The supplied sea class does not independently establish a river mouth, and no contemporary coast or glacier-front claim is made.

records.region: Sonora, Mexico: eastern dry tributary valley, hill-margin passage, southwestward alluvial corridor and Bahía La Salina coastal setting.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: No representative natural-river hydronym for the entire selected composite is supported by the actually read naming original. Named mountain and coastal features remain bounded observations.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The eastern chosen wash, upper hill-margin bend and westward fan, southwestward receiving corridor, modified middle land, lower alluvial/cultivated floor and coastal ending are geographically accounted for across all 16 stored parts. No separate-basin or missing receiving transfer remains in this bounded geographic reading. The naming original supplies only bounded neighboring/upland/coastal names, so the representative river name remains null.
records.completion_scope: All 16 selected parts have ordinary geographic correspondence from the interior dry valley through the alluvial corridor to the Bahía La Salina coastal setting. No representative natural-river name is established; river-name fields remain null.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative natural-river hydronym for the entire selected composite is supported by the actually read naming original. Named mountain and coastal features remain bounded observations.

scope_limits: A complete geographic reading does not establish a representative natural-river name. The finding remains a completed null name-scope hold, not an assertion that local people have no name for the drainage.

Alluvial fans and the lower cultivated/coastal floor contain multiple dry traces and diffuse passages. Ordinary connected receiving geography is supported; a single current wet thread, exact banks and present managed routing are not claimed.

The upper modeled bends are coarse relative to individual rocky spurs. The inspected valley and fan passage establish the ordinary geographic corridor without asserting every vertex lies in an active channel or proving present flow direction.
The municipal original clips out the Caborca portions; only imagery supplies those geographic observations. Listed municipal stream names do not fill the missing naming scope.
Source and render endpoints are separate recorded positions in the same inner coastal receiving setting; neither is asserted to be a surveyed natural mouth.
Satellite/aerial mosaic acquisition dates and present conditions are unverified. Formal registry verification and automatic application remain false.

records.region: South-central Alaska, Steller–Bering glacier complex, Vitus Lake and Seal River coast
records.candidate_name_role: No supported representative natural-river name over the full glacier–marginal-water–lake–river composite. Separate names are confined to bounded_name_observations.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Completed ordinary geographic correspondence for all three selected mainstem fragments: chosen high-ice opening, Steller Glacier and Lobe, connected Bering piedmont, western marginal-water arms, Vitus/Seal receiving waters, lower Seal River and separate coastal terminals. No single natural-river identity is established over this predominantly glaciated composite, so the whole-feature candidate remains null. The mapped river opening lies west of the generalized retained terminal points; this coastal-mouth offset is described rather than repaired or treated as an exact hydraulic route.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Completed ordinary geographic correspondence for all three selected mainstem fragments: chosen high-ice opening, Steller Glacier and Lobe, connected Bering piedmont, western marginal-water arms, Vitus/Seal receiving waters, lower Seal River and separate coastal terminals. No single natural-river identity is established over this predominantly glaciated composite, so the whole-feature candidate remains null. The mapped river opening lies west of the generalized retained terminal points; this coastal-mouth offset is described rather than repaired or treated as an exact hydraulic route.
records.completion_scope: This bounded research pass is complete at ordinary geographic scale, with a completed null naming-scope hold. No material lake/feeder transfer gap remains and no further acquisition is needed.
records.supported_name_scope: Steller Glacier/Lobe, Bering Glacier, Vitus Lake and Seal River are separately supported component names. No single representative natural-river identity is established for the full predominantly glaciated composite.

scope_limits: Ordinary continuous glacier/valley geography does not identify present supraglacial or subglacial flow, a natural river on the ice, current ice fronts or a glacier-name boundary for every position.
Lake arms, marginal waters and the broad Vitus/Seal complex are connected in the read cartography; changing lake level, ice retreat, water salinity and current flow directions are unverified.

The selected final segment crosses a generalized low coastal bar, while mapped Seal River bends west before opening to the sea. The distinct source/render terminal points share the outer coastal receiving setting east of that opening; neither is asserted to be the exact current river mouth.
The compilation provides regional geographic usage, not a directly verified formal name-register record. Its refresh date is not an individual-feature survey date.
A supported name for one component is not an alias for the glacier, lake or entire selection; no Korean form or automatic application is proposed.

terminal_review.observation: The first stage1 part follows the mapped southward lower Seal River toward its coastal turn. The original then shows Seal River turning west parallel to a low coastal bar before opening to the sea farther west. The selected final rendered segment instead continues south across that generalized bar setting. Its rendered terminal is at the outer coastal/marine margin east of the mapped opening; the distinct source terminal lies slightly farther seaward in the same coastal receiving setting. Both points were read separately against the original and a local orientation aid. The finding establishes their common outlet/coastal setting, not exact agreement with the active westward mouth or a hydraulic channel across the bar.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
